question: The diameter of a circle measures 25 cm. What is the maximum length of a chord in this circle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The longest chord of a circle is its diameter.

Given the diameter of the circle is 25 cm.

Maximum length of the chord = Diameter = 25 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the circle = 25 cm

**Concept Used:**

A chord is a line segment whose endpoints lie on the circumference of the circle.

As a chord moves closer to the center of the circle, its length continuously increases.

The chord that passes exactly through the center is the longest possible chord, which is known as the diameter.

 
 
• 
 Shorter Chord
 
• 
 
 Longest Chord (Diameter) = 25 cm
 Center O

**Calculation:**

⇒ Maximum length of chord = Length of diameter

⇒ Maximum length of chord = 25 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 25 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular from Center to Chord

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord perfectly bisects the chord into two equal parts.

Equal Chords and Subtended Angles

Equal chords of a circle subtend equal angles at the center of the circle.

Distance of Chords from Center

Equal chords of a circle are always equidistant from the center. Conversely, chords that are equidistant from the center are exactly equal in length.
